about.lead: When a foreign company looks at an ASEAN market, its first questions go to an industrial park, a law or accounting firm, a bank, a consultant or an investment-promotion agency. We write the research those teams need to answer.
about.storyP1: Each report starts from a question a foreign investor asks at a given stage. Is this market worth a look? How do we get in? How do we grow once we are there?
about.storyP2: We cover Southeast Asia, Australia, New Zealand and Taiwan. We focus on industries where foreign companies come to sell into the local market, not on export-only manufacturing.
about.storyP3: Our reports are desk research from public and licensed sources. Every figure carries its source, and our research team reviews each report before it is published.
about.pillar1Body: Reports are filed by country, industry and stage: explore, enter or expand. You find the answer that fits where your client is today.

custom.heroSub: Commission a senior analyst-led project tailored to your decision. Market entry, competitive deep-dives, partner landscapes, regulatory reads — typically delivered in 2–6 weeks.
custom.tierBriefingDesc: Targeted answer to a focused question. 8–15 pages, 1–2 week turnaround. Sized for a specific decision.
custom.tierStandardDesc: Full custom market analysis. Primary research, expert interviews, competitive landscape, scenarios. 3–6 weeks.
custom.tierRetainerDesc: Ongoing analyst capacity for strategy teams covering SEA. Monthly briefings, on-call analyst time, custom deliverables.
custom.processTitle: From brief to delivery in four steps.
custom.processSub: Every custom engagement runs through the same review-led process. No outsourced analyst pools, no ghost authors — your project is led end-to-end by a senior analyst on our team.
custom.step1Desc: 30-minute call to understand the decision behind the brief, current evidence base, and where the answer matters most.
custom.step2Desc: Written scope: research questions, methodology, sources, expert-interview targets, deliverable shape, timeline. Sign-off before fieldwork.
custom.step3Desc: In-region interviews, desk research, data analysis. Modern tools (including AI for synthesis) accelerate the work; senior analysts own the judgment.
custom.step4Desc: Final report, structured findings, and a working session to walk through implications. One revision round included.
custom.formSub: A senior analyst will reply within one business day. If your question is urgent, mention it below and we'll prioritise.
custom.briefPlaceholder: What's the decision behind this research? Markets, segments, players you're focused on. Anything we should know about context or constraints.
custom.successBody: A senior analyst will read your brief and reply within one business day. If you need to share more context, email hello@kiraresearch.com.

meth.titleLine1: How every report is researched, written and
meth.lead: Our reports are desk research. We work from public and licensed sources, tag the source of every figure, and review each report before it is published. This page explains each step and its limits.
meth.principle1Body: We work from published and licensed sources. We do not run fieldwork, surveys or interviews.
meth.principle2Body: We show where each number comes from, where we estimate, and where the evidence is thin.
meth.principle3Body: Every report is reviewed by our research team before it is published.
meth.step1P1: Each report is planned around a decision a foreign investor faces in one country and one industry. The stage sets the question: explore (is this market worth a closer look?), enter (how do we get in?) or expand (how do we grow after entry?).
meth.step1P2: Topics are proposed from our coverage plan and approved by our team before research starts. The plan lists the questions the report must answer, and the report is built to answer them.
meth.step1DetailLabel: What the plan fixes up front
meth.step1Detail1: The investor's stage and the decision behind the report
meth.step1Detail2: The guiding questions each section must answer
meth.step1Detail3: The analyses used to answer them (sizing, competition, entry routes, regulation, costs)
meth.step1Detail4: The scope: country, industry and, where useful, a narrower segment
meth.step2Title: Desk research from public and licensed sources.
meth.step2P1: We gather current data on market size, demand, competitors, regulation and recent deals before each report is written. Sources include government statistics, regulators, company filings and announcements, industry associations, trade and local-language media, and licensed data.
meth.step2P2: Where sources disagree, we say so. Where we estimate, we say so and show how.
meth.step2Detail1: A source tag on every reported figure
meth.step2Detail2: Local-language sources used for in-country data where available
meth.step2Detail3: Material figures compared across sources where more than one exists
meth.step2Detail4: An explicit "est." label on numbers we model ourselves
meth.step3P1: We use AI tools in our workflow: to search and summarise source material, structure data tables, draft sections against the research plan, and translate between English, Japanese, Korean and Chinese.
meth.step3P2: AI speeds up the work. It does not decide what a number is. Figures must trace back to a tagged source, and anything that cannot be sourced is removed or labelled as an estimate.
meth.step3Detail2: Drafting sections under the research plan
meth.step3Detail3: Building tables and charts from sourced data
meth.step3Detail4: Translating the English edition into Japanese, Korean and Chinese
meth.step4P1: Every report is reviewed by our research team before it goes out. The review checks that figures match their sources, that conclusions follow from the evidence, and that the report answers the questions it set out to answer.
meth.step4P2: Japanese, Korean and Chinese editions are translated from the reviewed English edition. Figures, names and sources stay the same across languages.
meth.step4Detail1: Reported figures checked against their tagged source
meth.step4Detail2: Unsourced claims removed or marked as estimates
meth.step4Detail3: Regulatory and market claims checked for currency
meth.step4Detail5: Final read for clarity and tone
meth.transLead: Desk research is good at some things and weak at others. Here is the honest split, so you know when to rely on a report and when to check further.
meth.transStrong1: Structured answers to entry questions: size, demand, competitors, rules, routes in
meth.transStrong2: Competitive landscapes built from filings, announcements and published data
meth.transStrong3: Traceable figures, each with a source you can check
meth.transStrong4: Consistent structure across countries, so markets can be compared
meth.transLimit1: No primary fieldwork: we do not run interviews, surveys or channel checks, so on-the-ground detail depends on what has been published
meth.transLimit2: Forecasts are estimates: directional, not precise to a percentage point
meth.transLimit3: Private company financials are often not public, and we mark estimates clearly
meth.transLimit4: Events after the last-refresh date are not covered until the report is refreshed
meth.qa1Body: Every reported number carries a source tag. Untraceable figures do not go out as facts.
meth.qa2Body: Our research team reads the report before publication. Weak claims are sharpened or removed.
meth.qa3Body: Language editions come from the reviewed English edition, with the same figures and sources.
meth.qa4Body: Each report shows its last-refresh date, so you know how current it is.
meth.closingBody: The method only matters if the reports stand up to it. Read any executive summary free and judge for yourself.
